subject: Re: Asterion Labs Order Form - pricing cadence, tax treatment, and net terms
messages:
From: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@asterionlabs.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@asterionlabs.com, Raj Patel <raj.patel@asterionlabs.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Asterion Order Form draft - questions on invoicing and tax

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for sending the draft order form — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few items our procurement and tax teams flagged as blockers before we can route to finance:

- Payment cadence: we prefer quarterly invoicing (to match our budget cycles). The draft currently shows monthly. Is quarterly compatible with Redwood's billing system?
- Net terms: Asterion requires Net 60 for this entity. Any flexibility on extending from Net 30?
- Tax treatment: we are a Canadian entity and will supply a GST/HST registration certificate if needed. The order form lists tax as "customer responsibility" but doesn't specify reverse-charge or a gross-up. Can Redwood confirm how tax will be applied and whether receipts will show tax separately?
- Proration / activation fee: if we ramp usage mid-quarter, how will proration be handled on the invoice?

I attached a short summary from our side (procurement_note.pdf) and highlighted the clauses we'd like clarified. Happy to jump on a call tomorrow.

Best,
Maria Gomez
Head of Procurement, Asterion Labs

Attachment: procurement_note.pdf (pdf)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@asterionlabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Asterion Order Form draft - questions on invoicing and tax

Maria — thanks, and great questions. Looping in Kimberly (Commercials) and Markus (Legal) to confirm the operational and tax implications. Quick answers below; I'll follow up with details and a redline: 

- Payment cadence: Redwood's billing system can support quarterly invoices, but we typically price on a monthly usage cadence. We can invoice quarterly by aggregating monthly usage; however, minimum commit recognition and proration rules will still apply per month unless we explicitly change the commit cadence on the order form.
- Net terms: Net 60 is possible for enterprise deals but requires approval from Finance. Ben, can you confirm whether Net 60 is acceptable for D-2026-AST-044 and whether there's any credit holdback or early-payment discount implications?
- Tax treatment: Markus — can you confirm whether we should be adding a reverse-charge clause or gross-up language for Canadian GST/HST? Also advise whether we need a formal GST certificate in the order form appendix.
- Proration: We typically prorate activation and any committed capacity on a per-month basis. If Asterion wants proration at the quarter level, that is doable but will change how the invoice line items are presented.

I'll attach our suggested redline to the order form with two options: (A) keep monthly commit recognition and quarterly invoices, (B) move commit cadence to quarterly (affects price bands and minimums).

Next steps: Kimberly to send the commercial impact (pricing spreadsheet) and Markus to provide the legal language. Maria, if you have internal deadlines, send them so we prioritize.

Thanks — Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Asterion_OrderForm_v1_redlines.docx (docx)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@asterionlabs.com>, contracts@asterionlabs.com
Date: 2026-08-16T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Asterion Order Form draft - questions on invoicing and tax

Hannah / team — flagged a few legal notes for Maria and Asterion's contracts inbox: 

1) Net terms: We can accept Net 60 with the following conditions captured in the order form:
   - Redwood to reserve the right to require a security deposit or an initial prepayment equal to the first invoice if credit checks indicate counterparty risk.
   - Late fee: 1.5% monthly after 30 days past due (or max allowed by law).

2) Tax language: Proposed clause: "All fees are exclusive of taxes; Customer shall be responsible for VAT/GST/HST and any applicable withholding taxes, provided that Customer provides valid tax exemption documentation where applicable. For Canadian GST/HST, Redwood will accept Customer's GST/HST registration number and apply tax treatment consistent with Canadian tax law; if a reverse charge mechanism applies, Customer must notify Redwood in writing prior to the first invoice."

3) Proration: Recommend keeping proration at a monthly recognition level for billing clarity. If Asterion requires quarter-level proration, we need to update price bands and recalibrate minimum-commit math; commercial will need ~24 hrs to run revised numbers.

4) Invoicing: We will provide itemized invoices showing gross fees, taxes, credits, and the total due. If Asterion requests a single consolidated quarterly line, Ops will need explicit formatting requirements.

I've added these comments inline in the redline (see attached). Happy to take specific wording suggestions from Asterion.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Asterion_OrderForm_v1_redlines.docx (docx)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@asterionlabs.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, contracts@asterionlabs.com
Date: 2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Asterion Order Form draft - questions on invoicing and tax

Maria / team — Ben here on Commercials / Finance. Quick update after a run of the numbers for the two options Hannah proposed: 

- Option A (monthly commit recognition, quarterly invoices): Pricing stays identical to draft; Redwood will bill every quarter by aggregating monthly invoices. There is no pricing uplift, and minimum commit enforcement remains monthly (we will include a one-line note on the invoice showing monthly commit compliance). This is the lowest-friction option operationally.

- Option B (quarterly commit cadence): To move to quarterly recognition we need to convert monthly bands into quarter-equivalents. That increases minimum exposure slightly because we round up to the next full pricing band for a quarter. For Asterion's target volumes, this results in a ~3.2% higher effective rate for committed capacity. If Asterion is comfortable with that, we can produce a revised order form and pricing appendix.

Net terms: Finance is willing to approve Net 60 for this deal provided we add the security deposit clause Markus suggested for new customers.

Next steps: Maria — please confirm preferred option (A or B) and whether Asterion will provide GST/HST registration details. If Option A, we can send final order form today and schedule execution. If Option B, give us 24 business hours to produce the revised pricing attachment.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference

Attachment: OrderForm_pricing_spreadsheet.csv (csv)
